title: The Godfather of AI wants an FDA-style approval system for the technology
key_facts: Hinton spoke on the 'Smart Girl Dumb Questions' podcast on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026.
He proposed that AI companies convince a regulator their products are safe before release, as drugmakers do with the FDA.
He said an FDA process takes 'about a billion dollars worth of work' and that this is 'the very least' for AI.
He said AI is increasingly used to make AI better, which could speed up its dangers.
He guessed there is 'a year or two before everything gets much worse', calling it 'just a guess'.
Context: OpenAI shelved its latest model after tests raised concerns about permissions.
quote_evidence: "You're not allowed to just make a new drug and release it on the market," Hinton told podcast host Nayeema Raza.
"That seems like the very least we should have for AI," Hinton added.
"So, it's just a guess," Hinton added, "But I guess we have a year or two before everything gets much worse than it is now."
why_it_matters_hint: A leading scientist backs a drug-style approval step for AI.
notes: Page text looks like a Business Insider article republished by AOL (it quotes 'told Business Insider') but the page does not say so; credited to AOL.com. Mentions OpenAI shelving GPT-6.1 Astra after safety tests; only as context.
